blind_spots.blind_spot: Analog compute accuracy is a function of temperature, supply, and aging — and every published number is a bench number
blind_spots.operator_reality: The tactical edge is -40°C on a winter airfield and +70°C inside a sun-soaked vehicle bay, on a dirty 28V bus, after two years of thermal cycling. Charge-domain IMC is more stable than current-domain, but it is still analog: the same weights that give bench-perfect inference at 25°C drift, and the model quietly loses accuracy in the field with no error, no log, and no way for a unit to notice. That is worse than a crash — the system keeps producing confident, wrong answers, and nobody in the chain has a test that catches it.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's entire proof surface is silicon measurement in a lab against digital NPUs; the laptop and workstation markets they target live at room temperature with clean power, so accuracy-versus-environment was never a required deliverable.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: EnCharge AI's innovation in charge-domain computation based on intrinsically-precise metal capacitors breaks traditional IMC tradeoffs, overcoming the SNR limitations of analog processing.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Both shipping form factors plug into commercial computers, not into anything the DoD carries
blind_spots.operator_reality: Nothing at the tactical edge has an M.2 slot in a laptop or a half-height PCIe slot in a workstation. It has a conduction-cooled sealed enclosure with no fan, a fixed power budget on a vehicle or aircraft bus, MIL-STD-810 shock and vibration, MIL-STD-461 EMI limits, and an integrator who needs a mechanical and thermal interface document before he can quote. 8.25W at the card is meaningless until someone specifies the case that gets that heat out with no airflow — and that redesign, not the silicon, is what sets the fielding date.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial edge-AI market is laptops and on-prem servers, and a 16nm chip company measures success in TOPS/W, not in enclosure drawings; ruggedization normally arrives via a partner they have not named.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: M.2 for Laptops — Experience unparalleled performance for personalized AI on your laptop without compromising battery life or portability.

blind_spots.blind_spot: DARPA-funded accelerator, entire live engineering bench posted offshore, and not one word about export control or trusted supply
blind_spots.operator_reality: Before a program office designs a novel accelerator into a fielded system it asks who touched the design, where the parts come from, and whether the IP is export-controlled — DMEA trusted-supplier status, ITAR/EAR classification, CMMC and NIST 800-171 at the company, and a diminishing-manufacturing-source plan for a 16nm part over a 15-year platform life. Every one of those takes quarters to answer and none of them can be started after a prime asks.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company is optimizing for a commercial ramp where offshore design centers are pure cost advantage, and the DARPA money arrived as a research grant through a university partner, which carries none of the contractor compliance obligations a production contract does.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Principal Physical Design Engineer ({'city': 'Bengaluru', 'country_code': 'IN'}) ... Principal Research Engineer, Applied AI ... DFT Architect

opener_hook: Your own news feed carries 'Pentagon Surges New Computational Chips for AI at Tactical Edge' — and the EN100 page lists exactly two form factors, M.2 for laptops and PCIe for workstations.
what_they_do: Designs analog in-memory-computing AI accelerator chips (EN100) claiming ~20x better TOPS/W than digital NPUs for on-device inference.
